programme.title: Three Little Words
programme.desc: In the Big City, true love is increasingly hard to achieve. But what if brave souls, yearning for romance and a loving partnership, agree to a provocative proposal: getting married at first sight? This groundbreaking format offers a shockingly novel twist on the relationship, dating and wedding space. Four experts - a therapist, anthropologist, spiritualist and clinical psychologist - will create what they believe are three perfect couples. The twist is that these couples will never meet or know each other until they walk down the aisle and see each other face to face - for the first time - at the altar. Each self-contained episode will track classic lifestyle stories of newlyweds: the honeymoon; early nesting; meeting the in-laws; and other universally relatable events of married life. Will they remain together in the end, or decide to separate?

programme.title: In A Family Way
programme.desc: In ARRANGED, three couples from different cultural backgrounds have one thing in common-- the belief in arranged marriages. From a Romani gypsy couple in New York City, to a southern couple from the Bible belt, to a couple raised by traditional Eastern Indian parents living in Los Angeles-- these brides and grooms don't just marry each other, their unions include their entire family. Viewers will see each couple's relationship from the lead-up to their weddings to the several months after the reality of married life sinks in.

programme.title: Love and Hate (#101)
programme.desc: Unconventional couples on their way to the altar face staunch criticism from loved ones who refuse to give their blessing and set aside personal prejudices about differences_x000D_ in race, religion, class, or sexuality. Whose family and friends will show up? And of those that do, will they voice their disapproval or forever hold their_x000D_ peace?

Each self-contained episode will track classic lifestyle stories of newlyweds: the honeymoon; early nesting; meeting the in-laws; and other universally relatable events of married life. Will they remain together in the end, or decide to separate?

programme.title: Happily Ever Arranged?
programme.desc: In ARRANGED, three couples from different cultural backgrounds have one thing in common-- the belief in arranged marriages. From a Romani gypsy couple in New York City, to a southern couple from the Bible belt, to a couple raised by traditional Eastern Indian parents living in Los Angeles-- these brides and grooms don't just marry each other, their unions include their entire family. Viewers will see each couple's relationship from the lead-up to their weddings to the several months after the reality of married life sinks in.

programme.title: Little Girl Lost
programme.desc: However shocking the crime, media headlines eventually fade, but for heartbroken friends and family, the memories and their longing for justice never do. Cold Case Files? produced by the team behind Investigative ReportsTM, digs deep into the past, following detectives as they strive to breathe new life into "cold" unsolved crimes. Armed with the latest DNA technology and with dogged determination, investigators seek new leads in hopes of bringing the guilty to justice decades after the crimes have been committed. Whether it's a man who was initially a prime suspect in his son's death, watching as the police begin to suspect his wife or the gruesome shooting of an elderly couple whose bodies were found in the woods, each episode features a different cold case.

programme.title: Maximum Overdrive
programme.desc: After a comet causes a radiation storm on Earth, machines come to life and turn against their makers. Holed up in a North Carolina truck stop, a group of survivors must fend for themselves against a mass of homicidal trucks. A diner cook, Bill Robinson (Emilio Estevez), emerges as the unlikely leader of the pack, attempting to find an escape plan for himself and the survivors, who include his boss, Bubba Hendershot (Pat Hingle), and a newlywed couple.

programme.desc: After his father, an assassin, is brutally murdered, Nick Gant vows revenge on Division, the covert government agency that dabbles in psychic warfare and experimental drugs. Together with Cassie, a teenage clairvoyant, Nick goes in search of a missing girl and a stolen suitcase that could be the key to accomplishing their mutual goal.

programme.title: I, Frankenstein
programme.desc: Two centuries after Dr. Frankenstein assembles and reanimates his creature, Adam is still living. He becomes embroiled in a war between two immortal races: gargoyles, the traditional protectors of mankind, and evil demons. Since Adam is neither human nor demon, gargoyle Queen Leonore and demon Prince Naberius each want him for their own purposes. It is up to Adam to discover his inner humanity and the reason for his continued existence.

programme.title: The Dawns Here are Quiet (English Version)
programme.desc: It is late spring of 1942, and World War 2 is in full swing. programme.title: Great Tank Battles
programme.desc: The third episode opens with Rommel's second offensive in North Africa. The scene is switched to North Africa following the continuous battle between the British 8th Army, the Desert Rats.

programme.title: Modern Warfare: Russia In Afghanistan
programme.desc: In 1979, the Soviets had ill-suited uniforms and inferior fighting tactics, and found it impossible to defeat the popular Afghan guerrilla army. They had underestimated their enemy and lacked the forces to win.

programme.title: The Attackers
programme.desc: Amidst WWII's war-torn skies, Soviet Major Bestuzhev defends the airdrome. A bond forms with comrade Zhenya, but facing overwhelming odds, they must protect their homeland, confronting fears in a narrative of sacrifice, courage, and camaraderie. As the air raid sirens wail, they delve deeper into the turmoil of war, discovering the true essence of duty and the resilience of the human spirit.

programme.title: WWII: The Price of Empire
programme.desc: Japan unprovoked invasion had plunged China into war and Europe had been brought to the brink of conflict. In Italy Mussolini introduced fascism to the political landscape and Hitler dismantled democracy. Their expansion threatened neighboring nations.

programme.title: The Amazing World of War Machines
programme.desc: The history of armed conflict is intrinsically tied to the history of civilization and Man's quest for the basic things in life. Over the centuries those weapons ranged from bow and arrows to armor, swords and chain mail. But one technological development left them all behind - the invention of gunpowder. Since then, the advances in weaponry have been both awe-inspiring, and frightening.

programme.title: Battlezone: The Korean War
programme.desc: A documented report of Communist atrocities in Korea, with scenes just released depicting the horror and brutality of Communism. Includes interviews with returned prisoners of war who were eye witnesses to some of these atrocities and Major General William Dean and General Mark W. Clark.

programme.title: My Grandparents' War
programme.desc: Kristin Scott Thomas's grandfather William served as a Commanding officer in the Royal Navy throughout WW2. He survived some of the most devastating battles from Dunkirk to D-Day but never spoke about his experiences. For the first time, Kristin uncovers how he saved thousands at Dunkirk and endured the horrors of the Russian Artic convoys. Kristin's journey is packed with revelation and emotion.

programme.title: Hitler's Last Secrets: Fatal Liaison - The Strange Affair of Adolf and Eva
programme.desc: The protracted romance between Adolf Hitler and Eva Braun began in 1929 and ended in 1945 in the bunker under the ruins of the Chancellery. Eva was Hitler's bride for less than 40 hours before she committed suicide.

programme.title: Helicopter Warfare
programme.desc: In the Iraq War, flying in the desert poses unique difficulties - the dust storm that accompanies every landing and take-off - and the lack of places to hide. When a young Royal Navy pilot comes under fire from a tank, he soon finds himself engaged in a deadly game of cat and mouse.

programme.title: The Amazing World of War Machines
programme.desc: Another basic building block of civilization and warfare is the ship. From the Second Millennia BC, ships were used to transport troops to battle. The Egyptians and Syrians crossed the sea to do battle, and when they weren't fighting each other, they would use their vessels for trade, exploration and probably a little piracy! From the 7th and 6th centuries B.C, formal navies appeared.

programme.title: Visions of War: The Korean War
programme.desc: Covers the United States involvement with Korea and testing of Korean weapons. John Ford directed this film which is the only color documentary made during the Korean War.

programme.title: Nazi War Criminals
programme.desc: Nazi war criminals are put on trial for their war crimes committed during WWII. This program covers various events from the Lublin Massacre, German atrocities in concentration camps and many others

programme.title: Battlezone: The Vietnam War
programme.desc: The combined US Forces offer advice to the natives of South Vietnam.

programme.desc: North Korea crosses the 38th Parallel and invades South Korea on June 25, 1950. The North pushes through initial defenses and captures Seoul and US and UN forces dig in at Pusan.

programme.title: Secrets of the Nazis
programme.desc: On September 1, 1939, Germany invaded Poland in a blitzkrieg fueled not only by tactics and technology, but also by Pervitin-crystal meth. Developed in 1938, this 'miracle pill' boosted soldiers' endurance and morale, becoming a weapon of war. Declassified files, including Hitler's medical records, uncover Project D-IX and reveal how meth shaped Nazi power and altered the course of history.

programme.title: WWII: The Price of Empire
programme.desc: Before 1941 was half over, the Soviet Union was locked in struggle with Germany. Before the year was out, humanity would be hanging on the fate of Roosevelt's great union, compelled to join the struggle by what he termed 'a date which will live in infamy.'

programme.title: WWII In Color: D-Day to Nazi Downfall
programme.desc: Germany's retreat continues as the Allies liberate France and Belgium. Montgomery's ambition to end the war risks more than his reputation as the push toward the Netherlands begins.

programme.title: WWII: Capitulation
programme.desc: May 8, 1945. While the Allied troops were parading through liberated towns to cheering crowds, the Second World War was in its final, apocalyptic hours. The weeks preceding the end of the conflict would usher in a new world. The Soviets, more powerful than ever, invaded conquered territories and terrorized survivors. The last Nazi soldiers attempted to escape their inevitable fates.

programme.title: David Jason's Secret Service: The Story of Britain's Rich Spy History
programme.desc: Sir David searches out Britain's eccentric amateur inventors and backyard boffins, who played a key role in the defeat of Hitler and created the machinery of 21st-century surveillance.

programme.title: Decisive Battles of Hitler's War
programme.desc: To Adolf Hitler in 1940, Britain was no more than an irritant on his periphery to his rapidly expanding Third Reich. He was correct in his assumption that Britain had been almost fatally weakened by the fight of Dunkirk. If Britain were to be subdued, there seemed to be no more auspicious time than 1940. The Luftwaffe had proven themselves invincible, which filled them with pride and enthusiasm.

programme.title: The Bomber: Terror of World War II
programme.desc: The Blitz shook Britain, but the Allies struck back harder with strategic bombing. Technology advanced-radar, gun turrets, and bomb sights changed everything. Civil defenses rose. After Pearl Harbor, the US joined in, bringing more bombers, more power, and a new level of destruction to the war.

programme.title: Battlezone: The Vietnam War
programme.desc: US Army film intended to familiarize US troops with the tactics employed by the Vietcong. Consists mostly of captured VC propaganda footage.

programme.title: The Crusade in the Pacific

programme.desc: Our patrols in probing actions... The attack on Hill 1179... The return of Seoul refugees... and more of the ceasefire negotiations. The Reggia di Venaria, which was formerly a barracks during Bonaparte's conquest of Italy, has been renovated, narrowly escaping ruin.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Ron and Nancy believe their historic Baltimore home is perfect. But the seller warns, 'I hope you're good fighters.' At first, they battle faulty wiring and strange plumbing issues. Then, objects move on their own, and Nancy dreams of an old woman laughing as their house burns. As the haunting increases, they realize their home is a gateway between life and death-and someone tried to seal it shut.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Childhood fear is pure, untempered by adult rationality. After his divorce, Steven LaChance dismisses his children's nightmares as stress-until he experiences chilling disturbances himself. Shadows lurk, screams echo, and an unseen force preys on them. He flees, but when another family moves in, he vows to help them. If you enter the spirit world, the spirits enter yours.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Living together requires balance, but Mike and Lisa aren't alone in their new home. Lisa's behavior changes inexplicably, and Mike grows desperate for answers. A late-night encounter with an invisible force convinces him they are haunted. He sets up surveillance, watching and waiting. What he captures shakes him to the core-are ghosts real, or is he losing his mind?

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Children often feel powerless in the face of the adult world. In Glen Burnie, Maryland, 10-year-old Billy Bean's life is already in crisis. He and his sister are attacked at night-pinned to their beds by unseen forces. Billy senses an evil presence destroying his family. As the attacks worsen, he fights to uncover the dark secrets of the house on Little Road before he loses everything.

programme.title: Mysteries of the Sphinx
programme.desc: Across the silvery Nile from Cairo in Egypt, in the shadow of the great pyramids, is one of the true wonders of the world. For nearly five thousand years its existence has been shrouded in mystery, controversy and uncertainty. How long has it been there? Who built it and when? Why was it built? Whose face is on it? Are there secret chambers underneath?

programme.title: The Egyptians
programme.desc: A two-month immersion in one of the greatest archeological missions to crack the secret teXts of Saqqara.

programme.title: The Egyptians
programme.desc: Built for pharaoh Khufu over 4,500 years ago, the Great Pyramid of Giza is the only one of the Seven Wonders still standing today - and is by far the most famous of all pyramids! Yet, this jewel still holds many secrets. Thanks to an exceptional behind-the-scenes access, we'll try to unravel remaining mysteries. Secret chambers have much to reveal about the origins of this stone giant!

programme.title: Decoding da Vinci
programme.desc: 500 years after his death, Leonardo da Vinci's painting is still just as fascinating. And yet, there are only 16 surviving canvasses attributed to him, some of which are unfinished. Through analysis of infrared reflectography, a technique that reveals the drawing beneath the layer of paint, the film underlines the prowess of da Vinci's work and captures its meaning and emotion.

programme.title: The Romanovs
programme.desc: The ascension of Catherine's son Paul following her death in 1796. Reigning only for five short years, Paul was then succeeded by his own son, Alexander, who reigned during the tumultuous period of the Napoleonic Wars.

programme.title: The Vietnam War: Unknown Images
programme.desc: For the first three years of the war, the U.S. Infantry had two very different missions to win 'Hearts and Minds' and to 'Search & Destroy'. Join U.S. combat cameramen as they are choppered in alongside the troops to capture the fighting on assault operations including Starlight, Cedar Falls and Masher.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths: The Odyssey
programme.desc: Odysseus and his companions are trapped in the Cyclops' cave. But he is a man with a plan. He carves out a stake and, after having drunk Polyphemus under the table, drives it into his one eye.

programme.title: We Were There
programme.desc: We Were There captures the voices of America's greatest generation, as they share their stories of duty, service, and responsibility during World War II. While the tumultuous global events of the early 1940's provide the backdrop for this film, it is the men and women recalling their personal stories who take center stage.

programme.title: Where is Hitler? A Hot Trail During the Cold War
programme.desc: Did the Fuhrer escape with a submarine to Argentina, was he living in Washington D.C. or is there proof that he committed suicide? FBI, British intelligence and German authorities followed every rumour, hint and trace. Previously undisclosed files, interrogation tapes, rare footage and photographs have been compiled in an attempt to ascertain the circumstances surrounding Adolf Hitler's death.

programme.title: Nazi Creatures
programme.desc: Hitler, Goring, Himmler: the three architects of the Final Solution. They, like many other high ranking Nazis, shared a fascination with the animal world. In the last days of the Nazi regime, Hitler risked his life every day, leaving the safety of the bunker to walk his beloved dog, Blondi. But the Nazis' interest went beyond love of their pets or the animal welfare laws they introduced.

programme.title: Angkor Rediscovered
programme.desc: Using the most sophisticated technologies in conjunction with research focusing on statues, casts, and documents handed down by Louis Delaporte. He was one of the first explorers of Angkor in the 19th century.

programme.title: Napoleon Bonaparte: The Egyptian Campaign
programme.desc: Exploring Egypt proved more challenging than anticipated. Between the cultural shock, divergence of interests between the military and scientific communities, the epic combat with Mamelukes and Ottomans, popular uprisings, and outbreaks of the plague, this was an expedition to remember.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths
programme.desc: Taking revenge against Prometheus, Zeus created the first woman - the beautiful Pandora. He gave her a manipulative and deceptive character, and subjected Prometheus to terrible torture. But although Zeus and Prometheus both shared a shrewd and cunning nature, they clashed fiercely. Prometheus wanted to be of help to mankind, and managed to convince Zeus to give them fire.

programme.title: The Destiny of Rome
programme.desc: Ten years later, the supreme strategist Octavian waged the naval battle of Actium against his former ally, who now had the backing of Cleopatra. Octavian put an end to Antony and Cleopatra's military ambitions and became the first Roman emperor under the name of Augustus. Witness the last moments of the Roman Republic, marked by this terrible duel between two men hungry for glory.

programme.title: The Egyptians
programme.desc: In Saqqara, Zahi Hawass and his team uncover a trove of sarcophagi from the New Kingdom and Late Period. With over forty shafts dug, they anticipate rich discoveries. As they scan and possibly open the coffins, unexpected secrets emerge, revealing glimpses into Ancient Egypt's past. Forensic techniques transport them back over three millennia, breathing life into long-buried individuals.

programme.title: The Viking Myths
programme.desc: Meanwhile, Kvasir (the being born out of peace) goes out into the world and answers all questions with ease. So much so that the two dwarf brothers capture Kvasir, murder him, drain his blood and mix it with mead: thus creating the Mead of Poetry, a metaphor for poetic inspiration.

programme.title: Europe - History Seen From Above
programme.desc: Before Spain was Spain, it was Hispania. Roman troops landed in Ampurias in 218 BC, bringing centuries of stability that reshaped the Iberian Peninsula. Roads, aqueducts, bridges, and great cities transformed the landscape, many still visible today. Hispania became a jewel of Rome, a vital economic hub, and a bastion of empire that produced influential leaders and governors.

programme.title: The Amazing World of War Machines
programme.desc: Once man moved from hunter-gatherer to crop grower and farmer, he needed somewhere permanent to live, and to protect his property. From earliest civilization, forts, barricades and battlements were an intrinsic part of the world. Some of the oldest defensive structures still exist, and date back to the days of Assyria, Egypt and Greece.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths: The Odyssey
programme.desc: Odysseus has been living out peaceful days with Calypso for 7 years. But waves of nostalgia wash over him, and the memories of his wife, his son and his island never cease to torment him. Hermes, sent by Zeus, under pressure from Athena, comes to ask Calypso to let the king of Ithaca leave.

programme.title: The Rise and Fall of Versailles
programme.desc: The life and loves of France's most famous king, Louis XIV. Dubbed the Sun King by his admiring court, Louis conquered half of Europe, conducted dozens of love affairs and dazzled his contemporaries with his lavish entertainments. But perhaps his greatest achievement - and certainly his longest lasting love - was the incredible palace he built at Versailles, one of the wonders of the world.

programme.title: Europe - History Seen From Above
programme.desc: The White Cliffs of Dover long signaled Britain's frontier. By the first millennium, the land was a patchwork of rival kingdoms. The Norman conquest of 1066 changed everything, ushering in an age of castles and fortresses that asserted both power and protection. These enduring monuments testify to centuries of conquest and the long forging of four nations under one flag.

programme.title: Maestros of the Camps
programme.desc: From Europe to Asia and America, music has been written in secret by prisoners of all origins and religions in the concentration camps of the Second World War. Professional composers or amateur musicians, they left gems in all styles and genres: songs and masses, sonatas and tangos. Written on toilet paper, by night at candle light, sometimes destroyed, most of these works have never been heard.

Her side dish is a Braised Escarole with olive oil, pepperoncino and garlic -simple and delicious.

programme.title: Lidia's Kitchen

programme.title: Eating In With Lidia

programme.title: Lidia's Kitchen

Vin Brulee is a mulled wine infused with warm spices; it's the perfect choice to warm up on a cold night.

programme.title: Lidia's Kitchen

programme.title: Lidia's Kitchen

She then prepares a flavor-packed Fusilli with Spinach and Herbed Ricotta, as well as Lagane Pasta with Chickpeas.

For a little extra run, she'll also show you some of her favorite fruity spritzers.

Today's recipes include a Pasta Primavera "New School," which her kids always loved growing up, and the classic Raspberry and Walnut Cookies, a beloved Italian American staple.
